checks: A pivot by t(h−h(y_e)) fixes the mark and keeps the continuous normal nonzero near zero. Minimization at each mark gives D_e^−≤0≤D_e^+ with both derivatives defined using signed t.
With normalized continuous margin s and tangential coordinate ξ, solving the pivot gives cutoff −t g_{e,0}(ξ)/(1+tb). The denominator stays positive and at least 1/2 for sufficiently small |t|.

A proper section has an interior point of the fiber. Extending the segment from that point through any relative-interior section point and using convexity makes the latter interior to the fiber, so the normal line crosses s=0 on both sides. For a positive-area supporting section, convex interpolation with an interior point gives a normal interval on the permitted side through each relative-interior section point.

Write g=g_{e,0}(ξ). The proper line has (left,right) derivatives (g,g). The empty-side interval ends at zero and gains max(0,−cutoff), yielding (min(g,0),max(g,0)). The full-side interval starts at zero and loses max(0,cutoff), yielding (max(g,0),min(g,0)). For g=0 both are zero. The closed boundary contributes zero line length.

Outside the section, a nonempty compact normal interval has strictly positive distance from zero and eventually gives zero derivative. Tangential section boundaries of positive-area cuts and projections of lower-dimensional cuts are null. The signed length difference divided by |t| is bounded in absolute value by 2|g| over the compact fiber projection. Dominated convergence and the finite fiber sum apply, with the same clipping on the one interval and counting on the single projected point for d=1.

On the three scalar ranges h<0, 0≤h≤1, h>1, the E difference equals respectively −h, 0, h−1 and the F difference equals h−1, −1, −h. These are δ and −1−δ, including the transition values 0 and 1. The P difference is −A. Thus 0≤D_1^+−D_0^− gives the exact inequality with the coefficient 1 on full-side area.

An endpoint in its fiber interior makes its section proper and gives positive (d−1)-measure, including counting measure for d=1. This argument allows both endpoints in the same fiber. For base-only h the integrands are constant on each labeled section.

overlap.comparison: The proof's fixed-body part of (5) contains the same one-sided clipping formula inside a projective orbit certificate. Its statement assumes an orbit minimum at one or more deepest sites and does not give the two-mark inequality for a common minimizer.

The old-fiber part of the moving-body response has the same two supporting signs. The accepted conclusion concerns continuation at tied contacts and equalized cap losses, while this lemma compares the endpoint pivots of a single common minimizing cap.

Section 2 gives the two-sided derivative with proper sections and null nonproper traces. Its Section 3 rules out two regular contacts. The new scope includes positive-area supporting sections and quantifies their distinct signs.

readability: E and F are determined by the sign of the entire fiber relative to the original closed cap. E captures zero d-volume even though the supporting face is included. The labels are unambiguous for positive-volume fibers.

summary: The exact one-sided clipping rates yield the stated full-side penalty and empty-side exterior requirement for each actual common minimizing cap.
